title: Can LLMs Anticipate Their Cruxes?
abstract: arXiv:2610.21006v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: To use language models to help us make decisions we would like to understand the rationale behind the language model's outputs. In principle, the language model provides its rationale as part of its text output. However, the sheer volume of text makes this hard to use in practice. In this paper, we are interested in extracting the cruxes that lead a model to recommend one action over another. We take a crux to be a sub-question that a model's rollouts disagree on, where changing its value may have altered the conclusion. A crux is therefore a property of the distribution of a model's rollouts, not of any one rollout. We consider three strategies of increasing computational cost. First, we just ask a model to identify, a priori, what the cruxes of a decision will be. Second, we have the model actually go through the process of generating a response and then extract the cruxes that arose in its reasoning. Finally, we generate many response

translated_title: 大语言模型能否预判其关键症结？
translated_abstract: 要让语言模型帮助我们做决策，我们需要理解语言模型输出背后的理据。原则上，语言模型会在其文本输出中提供理据，但文本数量庞大，在实践中难以利用。在本文中，我们感兴趣的是提取导致模型推荐某一行动而非另一行动的关键症结。我们将“症结”定义为模型多次推演之间产生分歧的子问题，即改变其取值可能会改变结论。因此，症结是模型推演分布的属性，而不是任何单次推演的属性。我们考虑了三种计算成本递增的策略：第一，我们仅要求模型先验地预测决策的症结将是什么；第二，我们让模型实际完成生成回复的过程，然后从其推理中提取出现的症结；最后，我们生成多次响应……
tldr: 本文提出将模型决策中的“关键症结”定义为模型多次推演分布上产生分歧、且改变其取值可能改变结论的子问题，并比较了三种计算成本递增的策略（先验预测、事后推理提取、多次生成）来识别这些症结。
en_tdlr: This paper defines "cruxes" as sub-questions that a model's rollouts disagree on—where changing their value could alter the conclusion—and compares three increasingly computationally expensive strategies (prior anticipation, post-hoc extraction from reasoning, and sampling many rollouts) to identify them.
